name: answer-me-with-html
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and DeepSeek Harness
short: Turns a complex answer into a one-page visual explainer, with diagrams and tables, from a short Markdown draft your agent writes.
what: When a question needs a picture, the agent writes a short Markdown draft and a bundled CLI turns it into one HTML page with flow charts, sequence diagrams, tables and charts. The README says this takes about an eighth of the tokens of hand-written HTML. Pages are single offline files saved in `~/.answer-me-with-html/pages/`, and it can also make narrated explainer videos.
who: People who ask their agent to explain systems, compare options or review code, and find long walls of terminal text hard to follow. For quick one-line answers it doesn't make a page.

steps.title: Install with one command
steps.text: It asks which agents to install into.

steps.title: Or add the Claude Code marketplace
Ask a question
steps.text: No setup is needed after install. The agent decides when a page is worth making, or you can say "explain it in HTML".

steps.title: Stop the browser opening (optional)
steps.text: Settings change with a command. This one stops pages opening in the browser.

watch: The skill tells your agent to make pages often, without being asked. Turn the browser opening off if that gets in the way.
If Node.js is missing, the skill has your agent offer to install it, and it should only do that after you agree.
Pages pile up in `~/.answer-me-with-html/`. Clear them with `am clean`.
The CLI checks GitHub for updates in the background at most once a day. The README says nothing about you is sent.
Code blocks can quote your real files. The skill says to check before you share a page that holds private code.
The README's recommended install has your agent read and follow an INSTALL.md from the web. Read that file yourself first, or use one of the commands above.
